- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 2–3 periods.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply +1–2% bias to early horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2) triggers downward bias: reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days, especially if price is rising.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-periods (last 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply -1–2% correction to final 5–7 days.
